title: PFAPA syndrome in childhood: factors related to the number of PFAPA-associated fever days.
summary:
"PFAPA" is an abbreviation for the typical symptomatology of the disease, which is characterized by the periodic occurrence of fever, aphtous stomatitis, pharyngitis and cervical adenitis . The average age at onset of symptomatology is about 3 years . It is believed to be the most common periodic fever syndrome in the non-Mediterranean region. The cumulative incidence was 2.3 per 10,000 children (up to 5 years of age) in a Nordic study.  Febrile episodes usually occur every 3-6 weeks and last 4-5 days, often reaching a temperature of 39-40.5 °C. During symptom-free intervals, children are typically symptom-free, and growth and development are unaffected.
Diagnosis of PFAPA syndrome is based primarily on clinical presentation, although the "Modified Marshall Criteria" may be consulted. For this, parents are often asked to keep a fever and symptom log.
Based on current research, PFAPA syndrome is believed to be a (psychological) burden for affected children and their parents and is often diagnosed late. The aim of this study is to identify factors related to the number of fever days in the context of PFAPA syndrome. Here, we would like to pay particular attention to the significance of heat or cold during fever episodes. 
Data collection takes place cross-sectionally with an online survey and optionally longitudinally with the documentation of the participants within the FeverApp.
